posts.author: Charibo
posts.body:
I'm having trouble getting the background of a custom face graphic to be transparent. I've tried using multiple image editors, making sure to set the white background to transparent. It shows up fine in the editor, but when I set it to an actor the background is again visible.
The color I'm trying to designate as transparent is white, and the editors I've used are GIMP 3 and GraphicsGale, as they were both around from projects before RPG Maker. I haven't really been able to find any posts about this problem, so I feel like I may be doing something wrong. Any ideas would be greatly appreciated!
So this is the base picture
This one is from before I discovered "opacity threshold". This may be where my issue is
And this one is after that discovery. The difference being, the previous image has transparency applied to the entire layer while the latter only seems to affect the background color.

posts.author: pawsplay
posts.body: I'd use GIMP to fuzzy select the background and just cut it. The opacity threshold is a useful editing tool but can't be relied on to display what you want, since those colors are present in the rest of the image; you can play with the level and edit various layers. However, i would use the brute force approach. Can't display what isn't there!

posts.author: Charibo
posts.body: Thanks for the recommendation! I'm not very well versed in image editors, so I'm a bit overwhelmed by all the options. But with something specific to try, I've got hopes for it. My rat will have a face!

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
GIMP can sometimes be a little funny about removing backgrounds--sometimes deleting the background will just make it the background color you have set in your toolbox (which defaults to white). If using the Color Select or Magic Wand tool to select and delete the white doesn't work, try selecting what you want to remove and then using Select > Invert Selection, so that you get the rat instead of the background. Copy the rat and paste him into a transparent document!
I don't know exactly why sometimes it'll let you delete a background to transparency and sometimes it won't, but it's a pretty quick workaround if it's being stubborn!

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
into which picture format do you store the face?
while Ace defaults to JPG, it is much better to use PNG - because JPG has no true transparency, and the color replacement transparency used by the engine for JPG has a lot of problems.
PNG hzas true transparency and works much better

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
Paint definitely got a huge overhaul. First with Windows 7, when they introduced soft-edged brushes, and then with Windows 11 when they added layers. (This is the part where I shake my cane and tell someone to get off my lawn, right? XD)
Andar is absolutely right--you'll want to save your resources as .PNGs! JPEG, even when you don't need transparency, tends to "artifact" around the edges and make pixel art look very blurry and messy.

Click to expand...
It has to do with PNGs. They have the ability to save alpha channel information and other things. It isn't often used but is theoretically useful. However, the main result is that it's easy to goof when combining layers in a graphical editing program, and that data can cause the images to have weird background stuff if you insert them raw into PDFs. You can see these artifacts sometimes in Windows preview images; I can tell where the creators of the official RTP resources in some cases cleaned up that background data but in other cases left it, even though it's normally invisible. That's also why some PNGs have black backgrounds in previews and others white, even though they are both transparent when displayed normally.
